brief.headline: Cut ₹28644/year off our biggest bottle SKU by matching the ₹1.87/NOS price we already pay Suraj Blow Plast, and switch to 15 days after receipt to free up ₹46539 in cash for us.

priceAsk.summary: Match our best price of ₹1.87/NOS on the PET BOT AMBER 100ML/25MM NECK 12.5G bottle — a 16.6% cut from their current ₹2.18/NOS.
priceAsk.basis: We already pay Suraj Blow Plast ₹1.87/NOS for the same bottle. TPAC is 16.6% higher. The market ask for similar PP caps is ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typically ₹0.85–0.95), so there's room to come down to our best price, especially at our volume.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days after receipt to 15 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹46539 in cash for us. Paying 15 days earlier is worth about 10.27% to them — the rate they borrow money at — so offer this in exchange for the price cut to ₹1.87/NOS.

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC is healthy — they made ₹637.48 Cr in sales last year, keep about ₹4 of every ₹100 they sell, and carry a strong [ICRA] A / Stable credit rating. But their cash is stuck for 79 days (same as similar firms at 79d), and they borrow money at about 10.27%. We're tiny to them — our ₹11.32 L is just 0.02% of their revenue — so on our own we have almost no pull. However, they do have GST filing delays and EPF payment delays flagged, and their Altman Z-score of 2.77 puts them in the grey zone (not distress, but not safe either). Bundle more volume, commit longer, or show them we're serious about qualifying Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second source — that's how we get leverage.

evidence.point: We pay Suraj Blow Plast ₹1.87/NOS for the same PET bottle; TPAC charges ₹2.18/NOS — a 16.6% gap.
Closing that gap saves us ₹28644 a year on that one SKU.
Moving payment to 15 days after receipt frees up ₹46539 in cash for us.
They borrow money at about 10.27%, so paying 15 days early is worth that rate to them.
We're only 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue — tiny customer, so we need a bigger stick (second source or volume bundle).
Their Altman Z-score is 2.77 (grey zone), and they have GST filing delays and EPF payment delays — not in distress, but not rock-solid either.
evidence.figure: altmanZ: 2.77, zone: grey, riskFlags: GST filing delays, EPF payment delays

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue — does pharma bottles, caps and preforms. Already a second source for us on packaging; health score B (65/100). The strongest backup if TPAC won't move.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue) with pharma containers and bottles; health score B (73/100). A robust second source to qualify for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Suraj Blow Plast PVt. Ltd.
alternates.why: We already buy the same PET bottle from them at ₹1.87/NOS — our best price and proof the market will supply at that level.

risks: We're only ₹11.32 L to their ₹637.48 Cr — 0.02% — so they can easily walk away. Don't push hard until we've bundled more volume or shown them a qualified second source (Manjushree or Mold-Tek).

Their Altman Z-score of 2.77 is grey zone, and they have GST filing delays and EPF payment delays. Pushing too hard on price and faster payment at once might squeeze them into real trouble — phase the asks or tie payment speed to the price cut.
The ₹28644 saving is small (our total spend with them is ₹11.32 L). Make sure the negotiation effort and any second-source qualification cost less than the saving.
Market backups (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are leads to qualify — not yet priced or audited. Verify before using them as a credible threat.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to grow our business with you, but we need your price on the 100ml PET bottle to match the ₹1.87/NOS we're already paying Suraj — and if we move to 15-day payment, can you get us there?
